mitochondrial Ca(2+) uptake is a highly regulated process, which is controlled by the activity of the mitochondrial Na(+)-dependent Ca(2+) exchangers (NCLX and MCU) in response to changes in the cytosolic Ca2+ concentration.
the mitochondrial Na(+)-dependent Ca(2+) exchangers are the major pathway of calcium uptake in mitochondria and are involved in the modulation of Ca(2+) signalling.

The main takeaway from our work is that
mitochondria are not just passive calcium stores, but rather play a key role as active regulators of cytosolic calcium signals.

the mitochondrial Na(+)(+)/Ca(2+)(+) exchanger is not a passive calcium uniporter as it was previously thought, but rather a highly regulated calcium transporter that is involved in the fine-tuning of the intracellular calcium homeostasis and in the control of mitochondrial bioenergetics.
